core_obligations: Choose an injective resolution (proof lines 11980-11988): take a quasi-isomorphism F^bullet -> I^bullet with I^bullet a bounded below complex of injectives, hence K-injective, so the internal hom construction represents R SheafHom(E^bullet, F^bullet) by the product complex (H')^bullet.

Compare the two double complexes (proof lines 11990-12003): because the terms of E^bullet vanish above some degree and those of F^bullet below some degree, the product in the definition of (H')^bullet is finite; both H^bullet and (H')^bullet are the total complexes of the double complexes with terms SheafHom(E^{-q}, F^p), and the natural map comes from a map of double complexes.

Conclude quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 12004-12022): the first quadrant spectral sequence of the double complex reduces the claim to showing that F^bullet -> I^bullet induces an isomorphism on the cohomology of SheafHom(E, -) for E a direct summand of a finite free module, which is clear for E finite free and hence follows for a summand.
proof_roadmap: Resolve the second complex by a bounded below complex of injectives and use the internal hom construction.
Identify both complexes as total complexes of the same double complex and compare them by the associated spectral sequence.
Reduce to the finite free case, where the induced map on internal homs is visibly an isomorphism, and transfer to direct summands.
difficulty_reason: The lemma extends the termwise description of the derived internal hom from strictly perfect complexes to bounded above complexes whose terms are direct summands of finite free modules (statement lines 11958-11977). The proof (proof lines 11979-12022) resolves the second complex by a bounded below complex of injectives, identifies both sides as total complexes of the same double complex, compares them through the first quadrant spectral sequence, and reduces the remaining statement to the finite free case. H2: one spectral sequence comparison with a finite-free reduction, written out.
